bib.title: 15 Horoscopes (Statistical Rethinking, 1st ed.)
bib.venue: book chapter, Statistical Rethinking (CRC Press), pp. 441-443

read.skipped: Footnotes 169-184 are not in the PDF, so the evidence behind each claim was not read. Year is not printed in the excerpt.

question: Why does statistical advice resemble horoscopes, and what in the wider scientific process, beyond the statistics, produces false findings and what can a researcher control?
contributions: Eight-part list of dynamics of scientific discovery that generate error
Openness workflow: pre-plan, mock analysis, register, analyze as planned, share data and scripts

results.claim: The Lancet's editor-in-chief wrote in 2015 that perhaps half of the scientific literature may simply be untrue.
results.setup: Editorial opinion quoted by McElreath, not a measurement; cited to support the claim that science has many failures.
results.quote: much of the scientific literature, perhaps half, may simply be untrue.

results.claim: Many published findings, even in top journals, cannot be repeated; McElreath ties this to the nature of significance testing and a high false-discovery rate.
results.setup: Qualitative; footnote 173 holds the evidence but is not in the excerpt.
results.quote: First, it is hard to repeat many published findings, even those in the best journals.

results.claim: As many as half of new discoveries may turn out to be false.
results.setup: Rhetorical restatement of Horton's estimate; no data in the chapter.
results.quote: when as many as half of them will turn out to be false?

results.claim: There were more false elemental discoveries than there are current elements in the periodic table.
results.quote: There were more false elemental discoveries than there are current elements in the periodic table.

results.claim: Fermi's claimed elements 93 and 94 were really a mix of lighter, already-discovered elements; those numbers now belong to neptunium and plutonium.
results.setup: Fermi (1901-1954) used as an example that false discoveries are not only by frauds and cranks.
results.quote: He discovered two heavy elements, ausonium (Ao, atomic number 93) and hesperium (Es, atomic number 94).

results.claim: Science is a population-level process of variation and selective retention, so most findings at a time can be false while long-term science works, analogous to natural selection.
results.quote: Science is a population-level process of variation and selective retention.

results.claim: The chapter lists eight dynamics of scientific discovery: theory quality, funding, measurement quality, analysis quality, peer review, publication, post-publication review, replication and meta-analysis.
results.setup: The author's own list ('nothing special about mine'), items (1)-(8).
results.quote: Here’s a list of some salient pieces of the dynamic of scientific discovery, in no particular order.

results.claim: If most theories are wrong, most findings will be false positives.
results.setup: Back-reference to the quantitative argument on page 51 (not in this excerpt).
results.quote: If most theories are wrong, most findings will be false positives.

results.claim: Low signal-to-noise designs give unreliable findings, not no findings.
results.quote: Poor signal will not mean no findings, just unreliable ones.

results.claim: Analysis not designed before seeing the data can overfit in ways regularization cannot reliably address.
results.quote: then your analysis may overfit the data in ways that regularization cannot reliably address.

results.claim: Recommended workflow: pre-plan research with the analysis, document it as a mock analysis, register it publicly, collect data, analyze as planned, document and justify changes, put data and scripts online.
results.setup: Advice for individual researchers; the one aspect McElreath says you personally control.
results.quote: Pre-plan your research together with the statistical analysis.

results.claim: The data and its analysis are the scientific product; the paper is an advertisement.
results.quote: The data and its analysis are the scientific product. The paper is just an advertisement.

limits: Three pages, an essay: no data or experiments; every figure is an assertion or quoted opinion.
Footnotes 169-184 hold the sources and are absent from the PDF, so claims cannot be traced from this file.
The list of eight dynamics is explicitly the author's own and unranked.
practices: Pre-plan the research together with the statistical analysis (p.443).
Document the plan as a mock analysis you would not be ashamed to share with a colleague (p.443).
Register the plan publicly, for example in a repository such as Github or a webpage (p.443).
Collect the data, then analyze as planned; if the plan changes, document and justify the changes (p.443).
Put data and scripts online for reviewers rather than providing them on request, except where privacy prevents it (p.443).
Design the analysis before seeing the data, since regularization cannot reliably fix overfitting from post-hoc analysis (p.443).
